channel.title: School-related IT Infrastructure
channel.description: Course script for School-related IT Infrastructure (teacher training in computer science and digital basic education). Author: Gerald Landl · Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 Documentation techniques This chapter is the continuous script on documentation. It follows the order of the sessions, so each technique builds on the previous one. The session chapters only refer here: this is where how to document is explained, while the sessions say what to document. All submissions go into the portfolio repository (private, pull requests) and are assessed with the assessment rubric. Why document? School IT is rarely run by one person alone, and rarely by the same person for long. Whoever leaves the school, goes on parental leave or falls ill takes their knowledge with them if it has not been written down. Good documentation Virtualization & Containerization Session: 05.10.2026 · Documentation technique: Markdown, Git and pull request workflow · Homework due: 18.10.2026 Schools run a few servers for many tasks: learning platform, file storage, directory service, print server, administration software. In the past every task got its own computer, today they run on virtual machines or in containers. This saves hardware and electricity, makes backups and updates plannable, and allows changes to be tried out safely. In this session you learn how virtualization and containerization work, when to use which technique, and how to build a Linux VM and a Docker service in a laptop lab. Everything runs on your laptop with free software. Networking I Session: 19.10.2026 · Documentation technique: Network diagrams and IP plans · Homework due: 08.11.2026 This chapter is still a skeleton. Learning goals Theory Guided lab Exercise (school scenario) Documentation task Homework (graded) Security and data protection Sources {class=“pages pages-tree”} Networking II Session: 16.11.2026 · Documentation technique: VLAN and permission matrices · Homework due: 22.11.2026 This chapter is still a skeleton. Learning goals Theory Guided lab Exercise (school scenario) Documentation task Homework (graded) Security and data protection Sources {class=“pages pages-tree”} Server Administration Session: 23.11.2026 · Documentation technique: Runbooks · Homework due: 06.12.2026 This chapter is still a skeleton. Learning goals Theory Guided lab Exercise (school scenario) Documentation task Homework (graded) Security and data protection Sources {class=“pages pages-tree”} Client & Mobile Device Management Session: 07.12.2026 · Documentation technique: Change logs for device policies · Homework due: 13.12.2026 This chapter is still a skeleton. Learning goals Theory Guided lab Exercise (school scenario) Documentation task Homework (graded) Security and data protection Sources {class=“pages pages-tree”} IT Security & Data Protection Session: 14.12.2026 · Documentation technique: Processing register (GDPR) and ADRs This chapter is still a skeleton. Learning goals Theory Capstone case study Exercise (school scenario) Documentation task Security and data protection Sources {class=“pages pages-tree”} About this book Author: Gerald Landl Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 The English version is machine-translated and reviewed by the author. German is the authoritative version. The content on data protection and youth protection is not legal advice. Assessment rubric Portfolio submissions (documentation tasks and homework) are assessed on four criteria: Criterion Description Technical correctness The implementation works and matches the task. Completeness All required parts are present. Documentation quality Clear, well structured, appropriate documentation technique. School-context reflection Data protection and security aspects are considered. Weighting and scoring scheme to follow.
